newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain's rate seen unchanged Tuesday - poll.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain's rate seen unchanged Tuesday - poll.

text.p: The Bank of Spain should leave its key money market rate unchanged at the current level of six percent at its regular repurchase auction on Tuesday, dealers said on Monday.
A Reuter poll of 10 financial experts showed all ruled out a change in the official rate on Tuesday, although they added it could be reduced in the near future.

Despite tame Spanish inflation data in January which came in at plus 2.9 percent year-on-year, the Bank of Spain left its key money market rate unchanged from its previous repo operation, disappointing some in the market.
A relatively weak peseta was seen as one factor postponing a reduction in the Spain's official rate.
The Bank of Spain last cut on January 16, when the key money market rate was reduced by 25 basis points to six percent. The rate started 1996 at nine percent.
